title: Heat-value selection raised mean coral cover in two Atlantic HeatCRD samples in 1998-2019
abstract: We tested how a requirement for a survey heat value changes the coral-cover sample. HeatCRD version 1 gave 24,291 sample IDs in the Atlantic and Pacific in 1998-2019. We compared all records with records that have a TSA_DHW value in two periods. In the Atlantic, selected mean cover was higher by 4.66 points in 1998-2008 and 1.28 points in 2009-2019. Changes in data-source shares account for +4.65 and +1.30 points. The Pacific shifts were +0.31 and -0.02 points. Equal site weights reduced the Atlantic shifts to +1.46 and +0.09 points. A known-depth filter nearly removed them. These are exact descriptions of selected archive records, not population estimates or heat effects. Missing dates, source loss, survey effort and depth records limit use of the selected sample. The package gives code, the sample panel, source terms, raw-data hashes, checks and a figure.

display.caption: All-record and heat-selected cover means, and selection shifts under three weight rules. Values describe the archive. They have no population confidence intervals.
